programs.title: Woman at the end of the world
programs.desc:
A series of reports presenting the customs and life situation of women living in distant corners of the globe.Journalist Martyna Wojciechowska once again sets out on risky expeditions to learn about the activities, passions and dreams of women living in different cultures.Stops in the third edition of the program include Samoa, Ghana and India.Together with her interlocutors, she experiences their joys and sorrows and participates in everyday activities.This allows her to understand contrasts and learn about different approaches to femininity in different parts of the world
During her trip to India, Martyna Wojciechowska meets a family who, according to Hindu tradition, takes care of the Karni Mata temple in Rajasthan.The religious building is inhabited by over 20,000 rats, which are the incarnations of clan members.Manisha and Diksha take care of the rodents and provide them with food.Martyna also meets Ćitra, who tells her about her first meeting with her husband and shows her the typical outfit of Indian women - a colorful sari.Then, under the supervision of a hairdresser working in the middle of the street, the traveler takes on the role of a barber.

While traveling through picturesque Polynesia, Martyna Wojciechowska meets another fascinating heroine.In Samoa, the role one plays in the community is more important than gender and appearance.Boys can decide whether they want to become men and heads of the family, or choose a different life scenario - become fa'afafine.This term describes people who combine features of both sexes.Martyna visited Vaitoe Toelupe, a 26-year-old fa'afafine who is responsible for coordinating rescue services in the event of various disasters, and after work she designs women's clothes.Alex K'Sua, on the other hand, is the first fa'afafine lawyer in Samoa's history.
